# Deliberate practice

Playing a piece from beginning to end ten times teaches the mistakes. Deliberate practice is different: I find the single bar that fails, isolate it and play it slowly, hands separately, until it is clean. Then I repeat it with a small increase in speed. Repetition without attention only makes errors permanent.

Scales and arpeggios are the daily exercise. I keep sessions short, twenty minutes of full concentration, and stop when the attention fades. The muscle memory built this way holds under pressure, because the fingers do not have to think.

Record the hardest passage on the phone and listen back. The recording is honest where memory is generous.
